intro: Welcome! In this lesson you listen to longer, clear speech: a colleague explaining a change, a lecturer's announcement, someone talking about a hobby, short news reports and podcasts. You learn to find the main point, to follow the signposts speakers use, and to take quick notes on the key information.
teachingNotes: Recap and build: from a2-listening-practical the learner knows four habits (read the question first and predict the answer type, listen for the key word, don't panic at unknown words, listen twice) and how to find the main point of a short conversation. Recap that in one line, then go further: longer clear monologues (40–55 words) about work, school and hobbies. Teach three questions in plain Indonesian: who is talking, and to whom; what is the topic; what is the main message (a change, news, what people have to do, or a reason). The main point is usually in the first one or two sentences and often repeated at the end; days, rooms and examples are details (rincian).

Signposts (kata penunjuk: words that tell you what's coming): First / Then / Finally (the order of the points); The main reason is / The most important thing is (the main point is coming); However / but (a change of direction: the new or true information comes after it); Instead (the new plan replaces the old one); So (the result, or what to do); For example (a detail, not the main point). Teach them as listening signals, not as new grammar: however = namun, instead = sebagai gantinya, so = jadi.

News and podcasts: a short news report gives the main news in the first sentence (what happened + where), then details (when, how many, how much), then what's going to happen next or advice (Drivers should…). News uses the present perfect for new news (has started, have left) and the past simple for details. A podcast starts with an introduction (the podcast's name, the host) and then the topic: 'Today's topic is…', 'In this episode, I'm going to talk about…'. Trap: the podcast's name or general subject, or last week's topic, is not today's topic. British 'programme' = American 'program'.

Note-taking: key words, not sentences. Listen for who, what, when (day, date, time), where (place, room) and numbers; write numbers as digits, short forms (Mon, Fri, 9:30, Rp 50.000) and simple symbols (→ for so, + for and). Notes can be in English, Indonesian or a mix. After a change (not Monday, Tuesday; however; instead) write only the new information. Number and time traps: thirTEEN vs THIRty, fifTEEN vs FIFty (stress at the end vs the start); British 'half past eight' = 8:30, but Indonesian 'setengah delapan' = 7:30; Americans usually say 'eight thirty'. 'The sixteenth' = tanggal 16.

Common errors to target: choosing an interesting detail (a room, an example, the old reason) as the main point; writing the old information that comes before however / instead / not; hearing 15 as 50 or 13 as 30; half past eight written as 7:30 (setengah delapan); taking the podcast's name or last week's topic as today's topic; trying to translate every word or write full sentences and missing the next idea. When a learner answers a 'main point' question with a detail, ask: 'If you remove this idea, does the message still make sense?'

Limits: A0–A2 grammar only (present simple and continuous, past simple and continuous, present perfect with just/already/yet/ever/never, going to, will, can/could, should/have to/must, zero and first conditional). No passive (use 'is closed', 'has started', 'is late'), no past perfect, no relative clauses, no reported speech, no used to. If a learner meets the passive in real news (was closed, were injured), say it's a later lesson and to listen for the key words around it. Listening texts are one voice, at most 300 characters (a short bulletin, a short podcast intro), clear standard English. Answers are short (a day, a number, a place, a reason in a few words): accept the meaning, not exact words.

keyPoints.title: The main point of clear speech
keyPoints.explanation: Ask: Who is talking, and to whom? What is the topic? What is the main message (what changes, what's new, what people have to do, or why)? The main point is often in the first one or two sentences and again at the end. Signposts help: the main reason is…, however… (the new information comes after it), instead… (the new plan), so… (the result). Days, rooms and examples are details.

examples.en: From next week, our meeting is on Wednesday, not Monday.
examples.id: Mulai minggu depan, rapat kita hari Rabu, bukan Senin.

examples.en: The main reason is the price.
The office usually closes at five. However, today it closes at three.
examples.id: Kantor biasanya tutup jam lima. Namun, hari ini tutup jam tiga.

id.title: Poin utama ucapan yang jelas
id.explanation: Tanyakan: Siapa yang bicara, dan kepada siapa? Topiknya apa? Pesan utamanya apa (apa yang berubah, apa yang baru, apa yang harus dilakukan, atau kenapa)? Poin utama sering ada di satu-dua kalimat pertama dan diulang di akhir. Kata penunjuk (signpost) membantu: the main reason is… (alasan utamanya…), however… (namun: info baru datang setelahnya), instead… (sebagai gantinya: rencana baru), so… (jadi: hasilnya). Hari, ruangan dan contoh adalah rincian (detail).

keyPoints.title: Short news reports and podcasts
keyPoints.explanation: News: the first sentence gives the main news (what happened + where), then the details (when, how many, how much), then what's going to happen next or advice. New news often uses the present perfect: has started, have left. Podcasts: first the name and the host, then the topic: Today's topic is…, In this episode, I'm going to talk about…. The podcast's name or last week's topic is not today's topic.

examples.en: Here is the news. A new hospital has opened in Medan.
examples.id: Berikut beritanya. Sebuah rumah sakit baru sudah dibuka di Medan.

examples.en: In this episode, I'm going to talk about learning English with films.
examples.id: Di episode ini, aku akan membahas belajar bahasa Inggris lewat film.

id.title: Berita singkat dan podcast
id.explanation: Berita: kalimat pertama memberi berita utamanya (apa yang terjadi + di mana), lalu rinciannya (kapan, berapa banyak, berapa harganya), lalu apa yang akan terjadi berikutnya atau saran. Berita baru sering memakai present perfect: has started, have left. Podcast: pertama nama podcast dan pembawa acaranya (host), lalu topiknya: Today's topic is… (Topik hari ini…), In this episode, I'm going to talk about… (Di episode ini, aku akan membahas…). Nama podcast atau topik minggu lalu bukan topik hari ini.

keyPoints.title: Notes on key information
keyPoints.explanation: Write key words, not sentences. Listen for who, what, when (day, date, time), where (place, room) and numbers. Write numbers as digits and use short forms (Mon, 9:30) and symbols (→ = so, + = and). After a change (not Monday, Tuesday; however; instead) write only the new information. Careful: thirTEEN vs THIRty; half past seven = 7:30, but setengah tujuh = 6:30.

examples.en: The workshop is on Monday the twentieth at ten o'clock in the main hall.
examples.id: Lokakaryanya hari Senin tanggal 20 pukul sepuluh di aula utama. (Catatan: Workshop: Mon 20, 10:00, main hall)

examples.en: The bus leaves at half past seven, not at eight.
examples.id: Busnya berangkat pukul setengah delapan (7.30), bukan jam delapan. (Catatan: bus 7:30)

id.title: Mencatat informasi kunci
id.explanation: Tulis kata kunci, bukan kalimat. Dengarkan siapa, apa, kapan (hari, tanggal, jam), di mana (tempat, ruangan) dan angka. Tulis angka sebagai digit dan pakai singkatan (Mon, 9:30) dan simbol (→ = jadi, + = dan). Setelah ada perubahan (not Monday, Tuesday; however; instead), tulis hanya info yang baru. Hati-hati: thirTEEN (13) vs THIRty (30); half past seven = 7.30, padahal setengah tujuh = 6.30.

guidedPractice.prompt: You hear: 'We usually have lunch together in the canteen. However, this week the canteen is closed, so we're going to eat at the restaurant next door.' Where is lunch this week? Answer in a few words.
guidedPractice.hint: The new information comes after 'However'. The canteen is the old place.

guidedPractice.prompt: You hear: 'I joined the badminton club last year. The main reason is that I wanted to meet new people in my new city.' Why did the speaker join the club? Answer in a few words.
guidedPractice.hint: Listen after the signpost 'The main reason is'.

guidedPractice.prompt: You hear: 'Here is the travel news. The toll road to Bandung is closed this morning. There was an accident near kilometre 97.' Which road is closed? Answer in a few words.
guidedPractice.hint: News gives the main news first: what + where.

guidedPractice.prompt: You hear: 'The meeting is on Tuesday the thirteenth.' Write the date as a number.
guidedPractice.hint: thirTEEN has the stress at the end; THIRty has it at the start.

independentPractice.prompt: A podcast starts: 'Hi, I'm Dimas, and this is Kos Life. In this episode, I'm going to talk about learning to cook when you live alone.' What is the episode about? Answer in a few words.
expected: learning to cook when you live alone
independentPractice.hint: Listen after 'In this episode, I'm going to talk about'. 'Kos Life' is the name of the podcast.

independentPractice.prompt: Write short notes (key words only, not a sentence) for this message: 'Please send me the sales report before five o'clock on Friday.'
independentPractice.hint: What? When (day + time)? Write the number as a digit.

independentPractice.prompt: You hear: 'I wanted to study medicine. However, my exam results were bad, so I chose nursing. Now I really love it.' What does the speaker study now? Answer in one or two words.
independentPractice.hint: After 'However' and 'so' comes what really happened.

assessment.prompt: Listen to Budi's message to his team. What is the main reason for the change? Answer in English in a few words.
assessment.listen: Hi everyone, it's Budi from the finance team. From next month, we're going to work from home every Friday. The main reason is the building work on the third floor. It's very noisy, so it's difficult to have meetings. On the other days, we're going to work in the office as usual.
acceptableAnswers: the building work on the third floor
building work on the third floor
it is difficult to have meetings
assessment.rubric: Correct: the building work on the third floor (or that it's noisy / difficult to have meetings because of it). Construction / renovation = 100. The right reason in Indonesian (renovasi, bising) = 70. 'Friday' or 'work from home' = 0 (that's the change, not the reason). 'the finance team' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Listen to the lecturer's announcement. What does each group have to do for the project now? Answer in English in a few words.
assessment.listen: Good afternoon, everyone. Before we finish, some news about your project. You don't have to write a report this year. Instead, each group is going to give a ten-minute presentation in class. However, the deadline is the same: the twentieth of November.
assessment.rubric: Correct: give a (ten-minute) presentation in class. The right idea in Indonesian (presentasi) = 70. 'write a report' = 0 (that's the old plan: 'you don't have to'; 'Instead' introduces the new one). 'the twentieth of November' alone = 0 (the deadline, a detail that doesn't change).

assessment.prompt: Listen to the news report. What happened in Bekasi this morning? Answer in English in a few words.
assessment.listen: Here is the news. Heavy rain has caused floods in parts of Bekasi this morning. More than two hundred families have left their homes, and they are staying at a school. The water is going down slowly, but more rain is coming tonight.
assessment.rubric: Correct: floods (caused by heavy rain). 'banjir' (in Indonesian) = 70. 'heavy rain' / 'rain' alone = 50 (the cause, not the main news). 'families left their homes' alone = 50 (a result, a detail). 'more rain is coming' = 0 (that's tonight, not this morning).

assessment.prompt: Listen to the start of the podcast. What is the topic of today's episode? Answer in English in a few words.
assessment.listen: Welcome back to Money Talk, the podcast about work and money. I'm Sari. Last week we talked about getting your first job. Today's topic is different: saving money. My main tip is simple: save fifteen percent of your salary first, before you spend anything.
assessment.rubric: Correct: saving money. 'menabung' (in Indonesian) = 70. 'getting your first job' = 0 (last week's topic). 'work and money' or 'Money Talk' = 0 (the podcast in general, not today's episode). '15 percent' alone = 30 (the main tip, a detail of the topic).

assessment.prompt: Listen to Pak Hasan and take notes. What time does the training start? Write the time in numbers, like 6:00.
assessment.listen: Hi, it's Pak Hasan. Some changes to the training course next week. It isn't in the meeting room any more. We're going to use room 314 on the third floor. It starts at half past eight on Wednesday, and it finishes at four. Please bring your laptop.
assessment.rubric: Correct: 8:30 (half past eight). 7:30 = 0 (the Indonesian trap: setengah delapan = 7:30, but half past eight = 8:30). 4:00 = 0 (the finish time). 3:14 or 314 = 0 (the room number).

assessment.prompt: Listen to Rina's message and take notes. Where is the class this Saturday? Answer in English in one or two words.
assessment.listen: Hello, this is Rina from the English course. Your class this Saturday is going to be online, not at the school. There's no electricity in our building this weekend. The class starts at the same time, ten o'clock, and I'm going to email you the link on Friday.
assessment.rubric: Correct: online. 'daring' (in Indonesian) = 70. 'at the school' / 'in the building' = 0 (that's the usual place: 'not at the school'). '10:00' or 'Friday' = 0 (the time and the day of the email, not the place).

material.title: From key words to the main point

blocks.text:
At A2 you learnt to **listen smart**: read the question first, guess what kind of answer you need (a number, a time, a place), listen for the **key word**, and don't panic at new words. At B1 the speech is longer: a colleague explains a change, a lecturer makes an announcement, a friend talks about a hobby. Now you also need the **main point** (the most important idea), not only one detail.

Ask three questions while you listen:
- **Who is talking, and to whom?** A manager to the team, a lecturer to students, a friend to you.
- **What is the topic?** The meeting, the project, a hobby.
- **What is the main message?** What changes, what's new, what people have to do, or why.

The main point is often in the **first one or two sentences**, and speakers often say it again at the end. The rest are **details**: days, rooms, examples.

id.text:
Di A2 kamu sudah belajar **menyimak dengan cerdas**: baca pertanyaannya dulu, tebak jenis jawaban yang kamu perlukan (angka, jam, tempat), dengarkan **kata kuncinya**, dan jangan panik kalau ada kata baru. Di B1 ucapannya lebih panjang: rekan kerja menjelaskan perubahan, dosen memberi pengumuman, teman bercerita tentang hobinya. Sekarang kamu juga perlu menangkap **poin utama** (main point = ide yang paling penting), bukan hanya satu detail.

Tanyakan tiga hal ini sambil mendengarkan:
- **Siapa yang bicara, dan kepada siapa?** Manajer kepada timnya, dosen kepada mahasiswa, teman kepadamu.
- **Topiknya apa?** Rapat, proyek, hobi.
- **Pesan utamanya apa?** Apa yang berubah, apa yang baru, apa yang harus dilakukan, atau kenapa.

Poin utama sering ada di **satu-dua kalimat pertama**, dan pembicara sering mengulangnya di akhir. Sisanya adalah **rincian** (detail): hari, ruangan, contoh.

rows.en: From next week, our meeting is on Wednesday, not Monday.
rows.id: Mulai minggu depan, rapat kita hari Rabu, bukan Senin.

rows.en: It's in the same room, room 7.
rows.id: Tempatnya di ruangan yang sama, ruang 7.

id.note: detail: di sini tidak ada yang berubah

rows.en: I love cycling because it helps me relax after work.
rows.id: Aku suka bersepeda karena itu membantuku santai setelah kerja.
rows.note: main point: the hobby and why

rows.en: For example, last Sunday I rode to Bogor.
rows.id: Misalnya, Minggu lalu aku bersepeda ke Bogor.

blocks.text: Two Indonesian habits make listening harder. First, translating every word in your head: in longer speech you miss the next idea. Second, choosing an interesting **detail** as the main point. Test it: if you remove this idea, does the message still make sense? If yes, it was only a detail.

id.text: Dua kebiasaan yang membuat menyimak lebih sulit. Pertama, menerjemahkan setiap kata di kepala: di ucapan yang panjang, kamu kehilangan ide berikutnya. Kedua, memilih **detail** yang menarik sebagai poin utama. Uji begini: kalau ide ini dihapus, apakah pesannya masih masuk akal? Kalau ya, itu hanya detail.

blocks.prompt: A manager says: 'Our office is going to close at three o'clock on Friday. Cleaners are coming to clean the carpets. Please take your laptops home on Thursday.' What is the main point?
options: The office is going to close early on Friday.
The carpets in the office are very old.
The office is going to close on Thursday.
blocks.explain: The first sentence gives the main point: the office closes early (at three) on Friday. The cleaners are the reason, a detail; the carpets aren't old. Thursday is only the day to take your laptop home.

id.prompt: Seorang manajer berkata: 'Our office is going to close at three o'clock on Friday. Cleaners are coming to clean the carpets. Please take your laptops home on Thursday.' Apa poin utamanya?
id.explain: Kalimat pertama memberi poin utamanya: kantor tutup lebih awal (jam tiga) hari Jumat. Petugas kebersihan adalah alasannya, sebuah detail; karpetnya tidak disebut tua. Kamis hanya hari untuk membawa laptop pulang.

id.title: Dari kata kunci ke poin utama

material.title: Signposts: words that show the way

blocks.text:
Speakers use **signposts**: words that tell you what's coming next, like the signs on a toll road. Listen for them, because they show you where the important information is.
- **First, … Then, … Finally, …** → the order of the points.
- **The main reason is …** / **The most important thing is …** → the main point is coming. Listen carefully now!
- **However, …** / **but** → a change of direction. What comes **after** however is usually the new or the true information.
- **Instead, …** → the new plan replaces the old plan.
- **So …** → the result, or what you have to do.
- **For example, …** → a detail, not the main point.

id.text:
Pembicara memakai **signpost** (kata penunjuk): kata-kata yang memberitahu apa yang akan datang, seperti papan petunjuk di jalan tol. Dengarkan kata-kata ini, karena mereka menunjukkan di mana info pentingnya.
- **First, … Then, … Finally, …** (Pertama… Lalu… Terakhir…) → urutan poinnya.
- **The main reason is …** (Alasan utamanya…) / **The most important thing is …** (Hal yang paling penting…) → poin utama akan datang. Dengarkan baik-baik!
- **However, …** (Namun…) / **but** (tapi) → arahnya berubah. Yang datang **setelah** however biasanya info yang baru atau yang benar.
- **Instead, …** (Sebagai gantinya…) → rencana baru menggantikan rencana lama.
- **So …** (Jadi…) → hasilnya, atau apa yang harus kamu lakukan.
- **For example, …** (Misalnya…) → detail, bukan poin utama.

rows.en: First, I'll explain the new system. Then you can ask questions.
rows.id: Pertama, saya akan menjelaskan sistem barunya. Lalu kalian boleh bertanya.

rows.en: The main reason is the price.
The office usually closes at five. However, today it closes at three.
rows.id: Kantor biasanya tutup jam lima. Namun, hari ini tutup jam tiga.

rows.en: There's no meeting on Friday. Instead, I'm going to send a short email.
rows.id: Tidak ada rapat hari Jumat. Sebagai gantinya, saya akan mengirim email singkat.

rows.en: It was raining, so we stayed at home.
rows.id: Waktu itu hujan, jadi kami tinggal di rumah.

blocks.text: After **However**, **Instead** and **not** (*on Tuesday, not Monday*), the old information isn't true any more. Many learners write the first thing they hear: the old day, the old place, the old reason. Wait for the end of the sentence before you write.

id.text: Setelah **However**, **Instead** dan **not** (*on Tuesday, not Monday* = hari Selasa, bukan Senin), info yang lama sudah tidak berlaku. Banyak pelajar menulis hal pertama yang mereka dengar: hari yang lama, tempat yang lama, alasan yang lama. Tunggu sampai kalimatnya selesai sebelum menulis.

blocks.prompt: You hear: 'The training isn't in Bandung this year. Instead, it's going to be in Yogyakarta.' Where is the training this year?
blocks.explain: Instead introduces the new plan: Yogyakarta. Bandung is the old place ('isn't in Bandung'), and nobody says Jakarta.

id.prompt: Kamu mendengar: 'The training isn't in Bandung this year. Instead, it's going to be in Yogyakarta.' Di mana pelatihannya tahun ini?
id.explain: Instead memperkenalkan rencana baru: Yogyakarta. Bandung adalah tempat yang lama ('isn't in Bandung' = tidak di Bandung), dan Jakarta tidak disebut sama sekali.

blocks.text:
**News reports** have a clear shape:
- The **first sentence** gives the main news: what happened, and where. *A new hospital has opened in Medan.*
- Then the **details**: when, how many, how much, who.
- At the end: what's **going to** happen next, or advice (*Drivers should…*).

News often uses the **present perfect** (has/have + the third form of the verb, like *has opened*, *have left*) for new news, and then the past simple for the details: *It opened at eight this morning.*

**Podcasts** (audio shows, often one person talking) start with an introduction: the name of the podcast and the **host** (the person who presents it). Then the topic: **Today's topic is …** or **In this episode, I'm going to talk about …**. Then come the points, often with signposts: *First, … My second tip is …*

id.text:
**Berita** (news report) punya bentuk yang jelas:
- **Kalimat pertama** memberi berita utamanya: apa yang terjadi, dan di mana. *A new hospital has opened in Medan.* (Sebuah rumah sakit baru sudah dibuka di Medan.)
- Lalu **rinciannya**: kapan, berapa banyak, berapa harganya, siapa.
- Di akhir: apa yang **akan** terjadi berikutnya (*going to*), atau saran (*Drivers should…* = Pengemudi sebaiknya…).

Berita sering memakai **present perfect** (has/have + kata kerja bentuk ketiga, seperti *has opened*, *have left*) untuk kabar baru, lalu past simple untuk rinciannya: *It opened at eight this morning.* (Rumah sakitnya buka jam delapan tadi pagi.)

**Podcast** (siaran audio, sering satu orang yang bicara) dimulai dengan pembukaan: nama podcast dan **host**-nya (pembawa acara). Lalu topiknya: **Today's topic is …** (Topik hari ini…) atau **In this episode, I'm going to talk about …** (Di episode ini, aku akan membahas…). Setelah itu poin-poinnya, sering dengan signpost: *First, … My second tip is …* (Pertama… Tips keduaku…)

rows.en: A new hospital has opened in Medan.
rows.id: Sebuah rumah sakit baru sudah dibuka di Medan.

rows.en: More than three hundred people visited it on the first day.
rows.id: Lebih dari tiga ratus orang mengunjunginya di hari pertama.

rows.en: Welcome to the show. I'm your host, Dimas.
rows.id: Selamat datang di acara ini. Aku pembawa acaramu, Dimas.

rows.en: In this episode, I'm going to talk about learning English with films.
rows.id: Di episode ini, aku akan membahas belajar bahasa Inggris lewat film.

blocks.text: Two traps. In a podcast, the **name** of the podcast (*Money Talk*) and **last week's** topic are not today's topic: wait for *Today…* or *In this episode…*. In real news you also hear forms like *was closed* or *were injured* (the passive, a later lesson). Don't stop there: listen for the key words around them. British *programme* = American *program*.

id.text: Dua jebakan. Di podcast, **nama** podcast-nya (*Money Talk*) dan topik **minggu lalu** bukan topik hari ini: tunggu kata *Today…* atau *In this episode…*. Di berita sungguhan kamu juga akan mendengar bentuk seperti *was closed* atau *were injured* (bentuk pasif, dipelajari nanti). Jangan berhenti di situ: dengarkan kata-kata kunci di sekitarnya. *Programme* (Inggris Britania) = *program* (Amerika) = acara.

blocks.prompt: A podcast starts: 'Hi, I'm Budi, and this is Weekend Kitchen. Last week we made fried rice. Today I'm going to show you an easy chicken soup.' What is today's topic?
blocks.explain: 'Today I'm going to show you…' gives today's topic: an easy chicken soup. Fried rice was last week's topic, and Weekend Kitchen is only the name of the podcast.

id.prompt: Sebuah podcast dimulai: 'Hi, I'm Budi, and this is Weekend Kitchen. Last week we made fried rice. Today I'm going to show you an easy chicken soup.' Apa topik hari ini?
id.explain: 'Today I'm going to show you…' (Hari ini aku akan menunjukkan…) memberi topik hari ini: sup ayam yang mudah. Nasi goreng adalah topik minggu lalu, dan Weekend Kitchen hanya nama podcast-nya.

material.title: Taking notes: key words, not sentences

blocks.text:
When you listen to a message, a lecture or the news, you can't write every word. Write **notes**: only the key words.
- Listen for the **five key facts**: **who**, **what**, **when** (day, date, time), **where** (place, room) and **numbers** (how many, how much).
- Write **numbers as digits**: 15, not fifteen. Short forms are fine: Mon, Tue, Fri; 9:30; Rp 50.000.
- Use simple symbols: **→** = so (jadi), **+** = and.
- Your notes can be in English, Indonesian or a mix: they're for you.
- After a change (*not Monday*, *however*, *instead*), write only the **new** information, or cross out the old one.

Example: you hear *'The workshop is on Monday the twentieth at ten o'clock in the main hall. Please bring your laptop.'* Your notes: **Workshop: Mon 20, 10:00, main hall + laptop.**

id.text:
Saat mendengarkan pesan, kuliah atau berita, kamu tidak bisa menulis setiap kata. Tulis **catatan** (notes): hanya kata kuncinya.
- Dengarkan **lima fakta kunci**: **siapa** (who), **apa** (what), **kapan** (when: hari, tanggal, jam), **di mana** (where: tempat, ruangan) dan **angka** (numbers: berapa banyak, berapa harganya).
- Tulis **angka sebagai digit**: 15, bukan fifteen. Singkatan boleh: Mon, Tue, Fri; 9:30; Rp 50.000.
- Pakai simbol sederhana: **→** = so (jadi), **+** = and (dan).
- Catatanmu boleh dalam bahasa Inggris, bahasa Indonesia atau campuran: itu untukmu sendiri.
- Setelah ada perubahan (*not Monday*, *however*, *instead*), tulis hanya info yang **baru**, atau coret yang lama.

Contoh: kamu mendengar *'The workshop is on Monday the twentieth at ten o'clock in the main hall. Please bring your laptop.'* Catatanmu: **Workshop: Mon 20, 10:00, main hall + laptop.**

blocks.text: Number and time traps. thir**TEEN** (13) has the stress at the end, **THIR**ty (30) at the start; the same for fif**TEEN** / **FIF**ty. British **half past seven** = **7:30**, but Indonesian *setengah tujuh* = **6:30**! Americans usually say *seven thirty*. Dates: *the sixteenth* = tanggal 16.

id.text: Jebakan angka dan jam. thir**TEEN** (13) tekanannya di akhir, **THIR**ty (30) di awal; sama dengan fif**TEEN** / **FIF**ty. Dalam bahasa Inggris Britania **half past seven** = **7.30**, padahal *setengah tujuh* = **6.30**! Orang Amerika biasanya bilang *seven thirty*. Tanggal: *the sixteenth* = tanggal 16.

rows.id: Kami menjual 450 ponsel bulan Maret, jadi kami akan merekrut dua orang baru.

rows.en: The bus leaves at half past seven, not at eight.
rows.id: Busnya berangkat pukul setengah delapan (7.30), bukan jam delapan.

blocks.prompt: You hear: 'The library is closing early today, at a quarter past four.' Which note is correct?
blocks.explain: A quarter past four = fifteen minutes after four = 4:15. A quarter to four would be 3:45, and a quarter to five 4:45.

id.prompt: Kamu mendengar: 'The library is closing early today, at a quarter past four.' Catatan mana yang benar?
id.explain: A quarter past four = lima belas menit setelah jam empat = 4.15 (empat lewat seperempat). A quarter to four = 3.45, dan a quarter to five = 4.45.

id.intro: Selamat datang! Di pelajaran ini kamu mendengarkan ucapan yang lebih panjang dan jelas: rekan kerja menjelaskan perubahan, pengumuman dari dosen, seseorang bercerita tentang hobinya, berita singkat dan podcast. Kamu belajar menangkap poin utamanya, mengikuti kata penunjuk (signpost) yang dipakai pembicara, dan mencatat info kuncinya dengan cepat.
suggestedQuestions: Bagaimana cara menangkap poin utama kalau ucapannya panjang?
Signpost apa yang menandakan info penting akan datang?
Bagaimana aku tahu topik sebuah episode podcast?
Apa yang harus aku tulis saat mencatat?

assessment.lmp-1: Dengarkan pesan Budi untuk timnya. Apa alasan utama perubahan itu? Jawab dalam bahasa Inggris dengan beberapa kata.
assessment.lmp-2: Dengarkan pengumuman dosen. Sekarang apa yang harus dilakukan setiap kelompok untuk proyeknya? Jawab dalam bahasa Inggris dengan beberapa kata.
assessment.lmp-3: Dengarkan beritanya. Apa yang terjadi di Bekasi tadi pagi? Jawab dalam bahasa Inggris dengan beberapa kata.
assessment.lmp-4: Dengarkan pembukaan podcast-nya. Apa topik episode hari ini? Jawab dalam bahasa Inggris dengan beberapa kata.
assessment.lmp-5: Dengarkan Pak Hasan dan buat catatan. Pelatihannya mulai jam berapa? Tulis jamnya dengan angka, seperti 6:00.
assessment.lmp-6: Dengarkan pesan Rina dan buat catatan. Di mana kelasnya hari Sabtu ini? Jawab dalam bahasa Inggris dengan satu atau dua kata.
